acceptInvite.ledeAdmin: as an admin. Choose a username and a password to join.

acceptInvite.addressInUse: {address} already has an ostra account. Sign in to accept.
acceptInvite.signInLede: Sign in with your ostra account to accept {inviter}'s invitation to {organization}.

reset.lede: Enter the email on your account. We'll send it a link to choose a new password.
reset.tooMany: Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.
reset.sentAfter: belongs to an account here, a link to reset its password is on its way. It works once, within {hours} hours.
reset.sentHelp: Nothing after a few minutes? Check spam, or ask your instance admin for a reset link.
reset.offLede: This install doesn't send email, so an instance admin makes reset links. Ask yours for one: it works once, within {hours} hours.
reset.newLedeAfter: . Saving it signs you out everywhere else, CLI sessions included.
reset.savedLede: Sign in with your new password. Every session of this account has been signed out, CLI sessions included.
reset.expiredOn: Reset links work for {hours} hours. Request a new one.
reset.expiredOff: Reset links work for {hours} hours. Ask your instance admin for a new one.
reset.usedTitle: This reset link has been used

reset.usedOff: Each link works once. If you didn't just change your password, ask your instance admin for a new one.

access.title: Access
access.lede: Who can open {project}, and what each person may change in it.
access.readOnly: Only {project}'s admins change who can open it.
access.openHint: Everyone in {organization} can open it and start tasks.
access.restrictedHint: Only the people listed below, and the organization's admins. Nobody else sees that it exists.
access.openNote: Everyone in {organization} is a member here. List someone to make them a project admin.
access.nobody: Nobody is listed. Only the organization's admins see {project}.
access.adminsLine: {names} always see {project} and can change it: organization admins see every project, listed or not.
access.adminsLineOpen: {names} always see {project} and can change it, whoever is listed.
access.rolesLine: A project admin changes its repos, boards, environment and access. A project member starts, drives and reopens its tasks.
access.restrictBodyOne: It disappears at once for the 1 member who isn't listed. Their running tasks here keep running, and they can't open them.
access.restrictBodyOther: It disappears at once for the {n} members who aren't listed. Their running tasks here keep running, and they can't open them.
access.openBody: Every member of {organization} can open it, read its tasks and start new ones.
access.removeRestricted: {project} disappears for them at once, and tasks they drive here lose their driver.
access.removeOpen: They stay a member of {project}, without a project role.
access.panelOrgAdminsNote: They see every project. They aren't listed here.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.lede: Every account on this install, in any organization. Make a reset link, or choose who runs the install.
accounts.pick: Select an account to see it, make a reset link or make it an instance admin.
accounts.adminsHelp: Instance admins set email and storage, and make reset links for any account. The role opens nothing inside an organization they're not in, and the last one can't give it up.
accounts.removeBody: {name} keeps every organization membership. Only the instance's pages and settings close.
accounts.removeSelf: You'll lose these pages at once.
accounts.resetHint: A link that sets a new password. It works once, for {hours} hours, and signs {name} out everywhere else.
accounts.resetShown: Shown once. Works once, for {hours} hours.
accounts.resetEarlier: The link made earlier stops working.
accounts.mailOff: Mail is off on this install, so {name} can't reset by mail.
accounts.mailOn: {name} can also reset by mail from the sign-in page.
accounts.mailUnverified: {name}'s address isn't verified, so a reset by mail can't reach it.
accounts.own: Change your password from your account.
accounts.grantBody: {name} will set email and storage, and make reset links for any account. It opens nothing inside an organization {name} isn't in.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.lede: Who did what in {organization}. Entries are never changed or deleted. What an agent ran is in each task's event log.
audit.ledeProject: Who did what in {project}. What an agent ran is in each task's event log.
audit.dataNote: IDs and settings only. Entries never hold prompts, ticket text or tokens.
audit.eventLogLede: What the agent ran and read in this task, with every tool call's input.

eventLog.recordHost: A record shows what the agent asked for, not what a program it built went on to read. This task ran on host, which has no box.
eventLog.recordBox: A record shows what the agent asked for, not what a program it built went on to read. The box kept the agent in its workspace.
eventLog.loadFailed: The event log couldn't be loaded: {error}
eventLog.nothingYetHint: Every message, tool call and approval appears here as it's recorded.

palette.noneHint: Search looks in titles, prompts, tickets, messages and the commands and paths the agents used. Not in thoughts or tool output.

page.lede: Every task you can open: titles, prompts, tickets, messages, and the commands and paths agents used.
page.placeholder: Search tasks, tickets, messages and commands
page.emptyLede: Type a word, a ticket key or a command. Typing repo:, status: or by: sets a filter.
page.noMatchFilters: No task matches {query} with these filters.
page.covers: Search covers titles, prompts, tickets, messages, and the commands, paths and URLs agents used. It doesn't search agent output or thinking.
page.tooLong: A search is at most 500 characters.

spend.title: Spend
spend.lede: What agents spent, counted at the key proxy and priced per model. Budgets run by calendar month in UTC: at {warn}% admins are told, and at 100% new tasks and turns wait while running turns finish.
spend.overTooltip: Spent after the budget was reached{on}: the turns that were already running.
spend.warnOne: {model} has no price, so budgets can't count it.
spend.warnMany: {n} models have no price, so budgets can't count them.
spend.warnTokens: {tokens} tokens this month aren't in these figures.
spend.warnTokensPast: {tokens} tokens in {month} aren't in these figures.
spend.noSpendEver: Spend shows here once agents run. Prices come from each provider and models.dev; a model with no price is counted in tokens until it has one.
spend.pick: Pick a project, a model or the organization's budget.

budgets.statusReached: Spent {spent} this month. Reached on {date}: new tasks and turns wait.
budgets.statusReachedNoDate: Spent {spent} this month. Reached: new tasks and turns wait.
budgets.statusWarned: Spent {spent} this month, {share} of its budget.
budgets.statusUnder: Spent {spent} this month, {share} of its budget.
budgets.statusNone: Spent {spent} this month, with no budget. The organization's budget still covers it.
budgets.statusNoneOrg: Spent {spent} this month, with no budget.
budgets.help: Each calendar month in UTC. A raise above what's spent lets the held work go, in the order it was held.
budgets.helpOrg: Each calendar month in UTC. It covers every project's spend, with or without its own budget. A raise above what's spent lets the held work go, in the order it was held.
budgets.belowSpend: That's below this month's {spent}, so the budget is reached at once and its admins are told.
budgets.removeBody: Its held work goes at once, and its spend stops being limited.
budgets.pastMonth: Budgets change only for this month.
budgets.invalid: A budget is dollars and cents, up to $1,000,000.

prices.sourceAdmin: {provider} · an admin set this price on {date}.
prices.sourceNoneLine: {provider} · neither the endpoint nor models.dev lists a price.
prices.group: Price per million tokens, in USD
prices.help: Applies from when you save. Spend already counted is never repriced.
prices.helpTokens: Applies from when you save. Spend already counted is never repriced, so these {tokens} tokens stay unpriced.
prices.required: Fresh input and output need a price.
prices.invalid: A price is a number of dollars, up to $1,000,000.

budgetWait.organization: The organization’s budget for {month} is reached.
budgetWait.unpriced: This task’s model has no price, so the budget can’t count it.
budgetWait.startsQueued: The task starts queued, and goes once an admin raises the budget or the month ends.

budgetNotice.warnOrganization: The organization is at {percent}% of its budget

memory.title: Memory
memory.ledeProject: What {project}’s agents get before they start, and can search while they work.
memory.ledeOrganization: What every project’s agents get before they start, and can search while they work.
memory.pick: Pick a note to see it here.
memory.emptyBody: A note is one thing every new task in {scope} should know: a convention, a command, a gotcha. Write one, or approve one an agent proposed.
memory.archiveBody: New tasks stop getting it. Tasks running now keep what they started with.

panel.organizationScope: Organization: every project’s tasks get it

note.lede: Agents in {scope} get its title in their index, and read the whole note when they need it.
note.secretFound: This note holds {found}. Memory never holds credentials.
note.controlFound: This note holds a model-control token. Memory never holds text that poses as a model’s instructions.
note.conflict: {name} saved version {version} while you were editing. Your text is still in the editor: copy what you need, then reload.
note.alwaysHelp: Every session starts with the whole note, not only its title.
note.archiveHelp: Archived, it leaves the index and search. Its versions stay.
note.versionsHelp: every save keeps the one before it
note.scanned: A note is text every agent in {scope} follows. Each save is scanned for credentials, and a note that holds one is refused.

proposalsList.title: Proposals
proposalsList.lede: What agents and members asked {scope} to remember. None reaches an agent until someone decides it.
proposalsList.mergeHelp: Its new version names this proposal as its source.
proposalsList.conflict: {name} saved version {version} of the note since you opened it. Reload to merge into the latest.
proposalsList.reachesNext: An approved note reaches the next session, never a running one.

confirm.drainBody: Its {n} running tasks finish. It takes no new task until an admin resumes it, through disconnects and restarts.
confirm.drainBodyIdle: It takes no new task until an admin resumes it, through disconnects and restarts.
confirm.resumeBody: It takes tasks again as soon as it's connected.
confirm.resumeBodyOld: It's one minor behind, so it takes tasks again after it restarts.
confirm.revokeBody: Its {n} running tasks stop at once, and each can reopen on another runner. It's disconnected and can't connect again. Runners that joined with the same token stay.
confirm.revokeBodyIdle: It's disconnected and can't connect again. Runners that joined with the same token stay.
confirm.revokeBodyOwn: Your machine can't connect again until you run ostra runner and sign in.
confirm.rejectBody: It's disconnected and can't join again with its key. The token it used stays active: revoke it from {pool} if you don't trust it.
confirm.drainBodyOne: Its running task finishes. It takes no new task until an admin resumes it, through disconnects and restarts.
confirm.revokeBodyOne: Its running task stops at once, and can reopen on another runner. It's disconnected and can't connect again. Runners that joined with the same token stay.

approval.title: Needs you · runner approval
approval.wantsAfter: . It gets no task until an admin approves it.
approval.footnote: Any admin of {organization} can answer. Rejecting revokes its key, and the join stays in the audit log.
approval.approvedOffline: Approved by you. {name} is offline: it takes tasks when it connects.
approval.rejected: Rejected by you. {name} can't connect again.

lede.online: A {executor} runner in {pool}. {busy} of {slots} slots busy.
lede.personal: Your machine: a {executor} runner, not isolated. {busy} of {slots} tasks at once.
lede.personalOffline: Your machine is offline: it takes tasks when it connects.
lede.offline: A {executor} runner in {pool}. Offline since {since}; its boxes keep working.
lede.draining: Draining since {since}: it takes no new task, and the ones it runs finish.
lede.drainingNow: Draining: it takes no new task, and the ones it runs finish.
lede.joining: Waiting for an admin to approve it.

page.notFound: This runner doesn't exist, or you can't see it.
page.httpNote: It fell back from WebSocket, and tries WebSocket again on its own.
page.internet: the agent has direct internet access
page.offerDocker: What it offers after keeping some CPU and memory for itself.
page.offerKubernetes: What its namespace's quota allows, or OSTRA_RUNNER_SLOTS when the namespace has none.
page.hostSlotsOnly: host counts slots only: no CPU or memory limit.
page.sizesNotEnforced: Sizes not enforced: update this runner.
page.consequence: Draining lets its {n} tasks finish and takes no new ones. Revoking stops them at once.
page.consequenceIdle: Draining stops it taking new tasks. Revoking cuts it off at once.
page.consequenceResume: Resuming lets it take tasks again. Revoking stops its {n} tasks at once.
page.consequenceResumeIdle: Resuming lets it take tasks again. Revoking cuts it off at once.
page.consequenceOwn: Revoking cuts your machine off: it can't connect again until you sign in again.
page.consequenceOne: Draining lets its running task finish and takes no new one. Revoking stops it at once.
page.consequenceResumeOne: Resuming lets it take tasks again. Revoking stops its running task at once.

version.behindHead: One minor behind the server: it runs tasks, but gets no resume command and doesn't enforce box sizes.
version.behindHeadUpdate: One minor behind the server: it runs tasks. Update it when you can.
version.fixImage: It came from the runner image, so it doesn't update itself: run the v{version} image and restart it.
version.fixNpm: Restart it: it installs v{version} at start, unless it was started with the pin off.
version.fixSource: Pull and rebuild ostra at v{version}.
version.fixAhead: Newer than the server: it speaks the server's minor until the server is upgraded.
version.fixOutside: It speaks protocol 1.{minor}; this server accepts 1.{low} to 1.{high}. Update it to v{version}.

install.npmNote: pins itself to the server's version at start

history.versionRefused: Refused: its version is outside the window

projectRepos.title: Repos
projectRepos.lede: Every session checks these repos out side by side, in this order.
projectRepos.addNone: No other repo the App reaches.
projectRepos.cantRemove: This repo can't be removed while a task that isn't merged, stopped or done has a branch in it.
projectRepos.removeRefused: Not removed: these tasks still have a branch in it.
projectRepos.orderBody: Sessions check repos out in this order, and the agent's instructions list them in it. The order changes nothing for a running session.
projectRepos.help: Drag a repo by its handle, or focus the handle and press ↑ or ↓. A repo you add joins each open task at its next session. A project holds up to {max} repos.

review.onlyUnlinked: Approved by an unlinked GitHub account
review.stale: The approval is of an earlier commit

palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Type a command, or search tasks

step.noReopen: No task of yours to reopen.
step.resumes: It resumes from its own session, with your message.
step.denyHint: Enter denies {key}'s request, with your reason if you give one.
step.answeredFirst: Someone answered it a moment ago.

stop.title: Stop {key}?
stop.body: The agent's turn ends now. You can reopen it later.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.footnote: Shortcuts don't fire while you type in a field or the composer.
shortcuts.everyAction: Every action is in the command palette

automations.title: Automations
automations.lede: Rules and schedules that start tasks in {project}. A rule starts each matching ticket once; a schedule starts work at set times.
automations.note: A rule never starts more than {n} tasks an hour. Saving a rule starts nothing: its dry run lists the tickets that already match.
automations.switchMembers: Only project admins turn automations on and off.
automations.emptyBody: A rule turns matching tickets into tasks. A schedule starts work at set times.
automations.emptyAdmins: Members see the list. Only a project's admins make rules and schedules.
automations.noBoard: Attach a board first: rules act on its tickets.

editor.lede: Saving starts nothing. Tickets that already match are in the dry run, to start by hand.
editor.ledePrompt: Saving starts nothing. The first task starts at the next occurrence.
editor.name: Name
editor.fiveFields: Schedules take five fields, without L, W or #.
editor.checkFilterNote: starts each match the rule hasn't started, up to {n}
editor.skipWhileOpen: Skip while the last one is open
editor.skipWhileOpenNote: an occurrence waits until the previous task is merged, done or stopped
editor.promptNote: sent as the task's first message; it never shows in logs
editor.filterNoteSchedule: the tickets it checks each time
editor.filterNoteRule: a ticket starts once, when it starts to match
editor.noBoardFilter: Attach a board to filter tickets.
editor.poolLabelInvalid: A label is a name and a value, such as tier:fast.
editor.labelWaits: No runner in the project's pools has {label} yet: its tasks would wait.
editor.approvalOff: off: a rule's tasks start on their own
editor.approvalOn: on: each task waits in Needs approval until a member approves it
editor.deleteNote: Its history and the tasks it started stay.
editor.deleteBody: It stops at once. Its history and the tasks it started stay.
editor.pausedLimit: Paused after {n} starts in an hour.
editor.readOnly: Only a project admin changes this automation.

dry.title: Dry run
dry.lede: What starting each would do. Nothing has started.
dry.needCondition: Add a condition to see the tickets that match.
dry.subIssues: Skipped: it has {n} sub-issues; start them from its page
dry.matchedBefore: Skipped: this rule started it before

skip.last_open: Skipped: the last task is still open
skip.hourly_limit: Skipped: the rule reached its hourly limit
skip.budget: Skipped: the project's budget is spent

summary.one: {n} task from {n} ticket. It starts as if started by hand, through the queue and the budget.
summary.other: {n} tasks from {n} tickets. Each starts as if started by hand, through the queue and the budget.

dry.promptNote: A prompt schedule starts one task each time. Nothing starts until the first.

history.ledeRule: Starts each ticket that matches {filter}, once.
history.pausedLimit: Paused at {time} after {n} starts in an hour.
history.pausedScheduleNote: Occurrences while it's paused are skipped, and none catch up when it resumes.
history.pausedRuleNote: Tickets that match while it's paused don't start, now or when it resumes.
history.pausedLimitNote: Check the rule's filter, then resume it.

band.skippedOpen: skipped: the last task is still open

reason.last_open: The last task was still open
reason.hourly_limit: The rule reached {n} starts in an hour and paused
reason.over_limit: Over the {n} a time limit: it starts next time

history.emptyRule: Nothing yet. A rule acts when a ticket starts to match after it's saved.
history.emptySchedule: Nothing yet. The first occurrence is {date}.

home.paused: {rule} paused after {n} starts in an hour

reason.hasSubIssues: it has sub-issues; start them from its page
reason.notOnABoard: it is on none of the project's boards
reason.noProfile: the project has no agent profile for it
reason.noProvider: no key has the profile's model

bulkStart.lede: Each ticket starts on its own. One that can't start doesn't stop the others.
bulkStart.footnote: Up to {max} tickets at once. Each goes through the queue and the budget like any start.

startsSubIssues.one: This starts {n} task, one for each sub-issue.
startsSubIssues.other: This starts {n} tasks, one for each sub-issue.

plan.startReason: On one of the project's pools, through the queue and the budget
plan.refineReason: A refine task: it reads the code and pushes nothing
plan.subIssuesReason: one for each sub-issue on this project's boards

reason.overLimit: It has {n} sub-issues, over the limit of {max}
reason.noLeaf: None of its sub-issues is on this project's boards

ticketParent.title: Parent ticket
ticketParent.overLimit: {key} has {n} sub-issues on {project}'s boards. ostra starts at most {max} at once: split the ticket, or start the sub-issues one by one.
ticketParent.noneHere: None of {key}'s sub-issues are on {project}'s boards.
ticketParent.elsewhereNote: Listed, never started here. Start it from its own project.
ticketParent.fromCache: Read from ostra's copy of the tickets: Linear didn't answer.
